verses.text: When Jesus had spoken these things, He lifted up His eyes to heaven and said, "Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son may glorify You.
For You granted Him authority over all people, so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him.
Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do.
And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.
I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
Now they know that everything You have given Me comes from You.
For I have given them the words You gave Me, and they have received them. They knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.
I ask on their behalf. I do not ask on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those You have given Me; for they are Yours.
All I have is Yours, and all You have is Mine; and in them I have been glorified.
I will no longer be in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to You. Holy Father, protect them by Your name, the name You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one.
While I was with them, I protected and preserved them by Your name, the name You gave Me. Not one of them has been lost, except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.
But now I am coming to You; and I am saying these things while I am in the world, so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.
I have given them Your word and the world has hated them. For they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.
They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
Sanctify them by the truth; Your word is truth.
As You sent Me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.
For them I sanctify Myself, so that they too may be sanctified by the truth.
I am not asking on behalf of them alone, but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message,
that all of them may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You. May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.
I have given them the glory You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one—
I in them and You in Me—that they may be perfectly united, so that the world may know that You sent Me and have loved them just as You have loved Me.
Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.
Righteous Father, although the world has not known You, I know You, and they know that You sent Me.
And I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known, so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in them."

context.author: Traditionally the apostle John
context.genre: Prayer — the longest recorded prayer of Jesus, often called the High Priestly Prayer, closing His farewell teaching and immediately preceding the arrest
context.audience: A broad, likely mixed Jewish and Gentile readership toward the end of the first century
context.setting: Prayed late on the night Jesus was betrayed, very likely in or just outside the upper room, after the Passover meal had ended, Judas had left, and the long farewell teaching of chapters 13-16 was finished.
context.custom: Passover was observed reclining at table with four cups of wine shared during the meal. Jesus' prayer here is often placed after the meal's close, in a setting already full of themes of deliverance and praise. The prayer is called "high priestly" because it resembles the priest who carried the names of Israel's tribes on his breastplate before God (Exodus 28:29).
context.timelineImmediate: This prayer sits at the hinge of the Gospel: everything before it is Jesus teaching His disciples, and everything after it — beginning with the arrest in chapter 18 — is the Passion. It moves outward in three circles: Jesus prays for Himself, then for the eleven disciples, then for everyone who will ever believe through their message.
context.timelineBible: Jesus prays for those "who will believe in Me through their message" — a clear look forward to the generations of believers that would follow the apostles, and the reason this prayer has been read as covering every later follower, not just the disciples in the room.
context.sparkNotes: On the night He is betrayed, Jesus lifts His eyes and prays aloud in three widening circles: first for Himself, asking to be glorified so that He can glorify the Father; then for the disciples, asking that they be protected, sanctified by the truth, and sent into the world as He was sent; and finally for everyone who will believe through their message. The prayer's repeated request is unity — that believers be one as Jesus and the Father are one, so that the world may believe — and it closes with Jesus' desire that the love the Father has for Him would be in them.

translation.meaning: Jesus gives a definition here that is easy to miss: eternal life is not primarily described as endless duration, but as knowing "the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent" — a life defined by relationship and knowledge.

To set apart for God's purposes. Jesus asks that the disciples be sanctified by the truth, then says He sanctifies Himself for their sake — the same word applied to both, with the result that they too may be truly set apart.

The unity Jesus asks for is modeled on His unity with the Father — and strikingly, He asks that believers be "one as We are one," and that they be "in Us." The same word is used for the unity believers are invited into, which points to a relational unity of purpose and love.

otBackground.note: The high priest carrying the names of Israel's tribes over his heart into God's presence — the picture behind calling this the High Priestly Prayer.
God revealing His name to Moses — background for Jesus' repeated statement that He has made the Father's name known.
The priestly blessing, a pattern of a priest speaking God's care over His people.

commentary.note: Henry reads "this is eternal life, that they may know You" as describing both a present reality and a future one: now it is a "believing knowledge" of God and Christ, later it will be direct knowledge. Those who already live in communion with God, he says, are "in the suburbs of life eternal" and know by experience what it is — "if this be heaven, heaven is sweet."

On "sanctify them by the truth," Henry clarifies that the word does not sanctify on its own — otherwise it would always work — but is the instrument the Spirit commonly uses, being "the seed of the new birth" and "the food of the new life." He also reads the request as setting the disciples apart for their office, the way the Levitical priests were consecrated, but "really, not ritually."

Spurgeon turns verse 3 into a pointed personal question: "Do you know God? Do you know Jesus Christ? Are you on speaking terms, on loving terms, with them? Are they your friends? Then you have eternal life." For him the definition is less a doctrine to debate than a relationship to check.

overview.summary: Jesus lifts His eyes and prays. He asks the Father to glorify the Son, to protect and sanctify His disciples, and that all who believe through them would be one.
overview.settingLine: Spoken aloud before leaving the upper room.

history.t: Jesus prays knowing the cross is hours away.
The high priest carried Israel's names on his heart, as Jesus does in prayer.

customs.t: Jews often prayed with eyes lifted toward heaven.
God's name stood for His character and presence.

archaeology.t: Breastplate stones of twelve tribes are described in Exodus 28.
Tiny silver scrolls near Jerusalem carry the priestly blessing from about 600 BC.

overview.discussion: Jesus prayed that His followers would be one. What keeps believers divided today?
